JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but my problem is that the commander told you, the question itself revealed that you were wondering what the reason was and that's why he responded, why he told you, well, the building is on the confrontation line. The problem is that if you were aware of the fact that there were forces who were gathering or getting prepared in this building, it would have been normal for this building to be shelled so your question shows that you wanted to find out about this. I don't know if I'm clear. Is my question clear or would you like me to be more specific, elaborate on it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have described this building a number of times and the building was being used by snipers which were firing at Nedzarici, that is why the fire came back at the buildings and that is why the civilians moved from the front apartments to the rear apartments. Mine was a rear apartment. But I mean there were armoured personnel carriers, there were lots, lots of -- I mean a great number of soldiers and they were fighters for the Presidency side who were -- who formed up behind these buildings and then attacked Nedzarici. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, but my problem is that I still have the same problem. The question is: Since you were aware of all these details, why did you, yourself, as a military man, why did you ask the Serbian commander the reason for which he had shelled this building, given that on the basis of your testimony, it's obvious that it was a military target and it was quite normal for this building to be targeted? What I myself don't understand, since I'm not a military person, I don't understand -- the question that you put to the commander, you wanted to know the reason for which the building had been shelled but you are quite aware of the fact that it was a military target. So I want to know why you put this question to the Serbian commander.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I understand your question. The reason that I put the question to the deputy commander for Nedzarici was that we had UN flags hanging outside the buildings in clear view of the forces in Nedzarici so they knew that UN personnel were actually living in those buildings. That was the reason why I asked them. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but my question stands because you were aware of the fact that it was a military target and that it was legitimate to shell it and this is why your question seemed to me to be something that I couldn't understand but I'll move on to another subject. You said that in relation to the bombing or the bomb that was planted at the market, you said that you sent two of your officers there, a Canadian and an Australian in order to carry out an investigation. My question is: Was it customary, was it a rule, was it the rule that after each bombing, a UN commission would be formed and an investigation would be carried out, there would be a report for each incident or was this not customary and did you decide to launch an investigation into this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was customary that for -- because this had I mean so much media attention. I mean routine shelling did not attract this sort of attention by the UN. I mean it -- shelling was shelling and so -- but this one was specific and it was important that because of the attention that had been given to it by the media, that we actually had a very, very close look at it. Some of the shelling that happened was outside the view of -- I mean we could see it, but I mean it was outside the immediate area that we could actually attend and provide attention to or investigate, but this one was very close to the PTT. It received a lot of media attention and so it was thoroughly investigated and reports were given to Zagreb and the UN headquarters in New York. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So if I understand you correctly, a certain period of time elapsed between the incident and the response of the media -- yes, you were about to say?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that the media were there almost -- I mean they were there immediately. I mean they were there -- I mean they took photos. I mean it -- I'm sure it's on one of the videotapes. They were there almost as it happened and they were lucky that they were not actually injured or killed in the actual incident. They were there immediately and my officers who went there to investigate it, they were there within an hour, hour and a half, maximum. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Right, to avoid any misunderstanding, you are saying that your reaction was due or was egged on by the media because the media were reporting the incident and that you then reacted -- and you reacted then. So I presume that normally there should be an interval but that you actually were abreast of what the media were saying and therefore, your decision came to send officers to investigate the accident. I was asking you and you said that no, it was immediately. From what you remember, how long -- how much time elapsed between the incident and your intervention?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably an hour, an hour and a half between -- the media had satellite dishes, I mean they were -- they would take something from an incident and they would take it immediate -- the television building is immediately adjacent to the PTT and those pictures -- plus they also had a satellite dish set up at the PTT as well. So I mean those images were beamed out almost immediately that something had happened, and I mean we could -- we could watch it on the TV that I had in the PTT and it was important not only because of that but -- I mean I was directed to get an investigation team there as soon as possible and so that's when I sent the Australian artillery officer and the Canadian mortar officer, I sent them there immediately to do an investigation as people were still mopping up the blood and clearing away people. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Right, but were they the same officers whom you sent whenever something happened? What I mean is did they conduct other investigations prior to that particular incident or was it, from what you can remember, the first time they did that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think it was the -- probably the first time they did it and then the 13th of July incident happened after that. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Right. Now, I'd like to move on to another subject and that has to do with the incident which took place on the day when Sir Douglas Hurd arrived in Sarajevo. I'd like to understand you correctly. You said that you were in front of the door at the Presidency and that you heard shots, that is the impact, the primaries, I believe is the term, the English term is primaries, so you heard them and you were able to identify the firing point at a distance of 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was less than that. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] How much?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that it may have been 50, 75 metres away, maximum. I could hear them -- they were -- they were -- I mean the mortars were down a side street just by the Presidency, okay, and they fired directly over a building and they -- you have to hear a primary to actually know what it sounds like but I mean it is very distinctive. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Right. So they were behind a building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And you thought that in order to hear that sound, how many seconds does it take to get the sound, that is, what I mean is after how many seconds did you hear the impact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you're firing a mortar bomb just on the primary cartridge which is actually inside the base of the actual mortar bomb, and you're only firing it on primary and it goes maximum 200 metres, the time of flight is probably about 10 seconds. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Right. And you therefore heard it one, two seconds after the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I heard the primary -- I mean the people who were standing with me right at the front entrance, they moved inside because they knew that something was going to happen. The police, they weren't soldiers, they were police, who were forming the so-called honour guard -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, witness, to interrupt you, but I merely wanted or rather I wanted you to establish material facts of this because you made a value judgement. You said people knew and that is why they retreated but if we only keep to what happened, just that, nothing else, you said that you heard -- that you had heard what one calls a primary and then after -- and after that, how long -- how much time did elapse before you saw the explosion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about five or ten seconds. It was a very short distance away. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So in point of fact, you could not -- you could hear only one primary because the second one was launched immediately after it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were two primaries. I mean there were two bombs that landed. One landed -- one landed and then approximately 30 seconds later, another bomb landed. The people who were trying to actually help the person who was in the Mercedes, they were caught by the second bomb and then about 30 seconds later, from nowhere, an ambulance arrived and picked up all of the bodies and took them away to Kosovo hospital. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And during that time, you stayed in the front entrance of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] My last question is you answered it already, but I'd like to make sure, I'd like to make sure. You, personally, were you targeted personally or were you targeted as a representative of the United Nations? That is, was it your person or were you the -- a member, a representative of the United Nations, what is your feeling about it? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to your question is that I was targeted personally, I have given death threats -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but were you, as yourself or because you were representing an international organisation? Was it your personality or was it because you were a representative of the United Nations or was it you yourself?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was both because, I mean, I deliberately arranged for a cease-fire with the warring sides and they knew precisely at what time I was travelling across the airport to go to Lukavica to actually have a meeting. They knew that precisely. They knew I would be in the armoured personnel carrier and they deliberately fired at me. That was a personal attack. On other occasions, I was targeted because I was part of the UN body in UNPROFOR in Sarajevo. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So you cannot really distinguish, was it your person that was targeted or was it as a representative of the UN that you are targeted, is that your answer that you cannot really say whether there was any difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean there was a lot of difference when you're getting fired at. I mean the thing is that on certain occasions, the warring parties were totally clear on where I was and what I was doing and they deliberately fired at me. That is deliberate. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but you explained that after you arrived, you were able to acquire a picture of what was going on on the ground and that one party to the conflict was defending its rights, you said that the Serbs were defending their land and that the other party was attempting ethnic cleansing. Now, this value judgement, if I may put it that way, was it being done -- can that explain, that is the knowledge of the two parties, could that explain then the given attitude?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well do. But I mean again, that is, I mean, a value judgment. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I've got a few questions for you as well.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]

utterances.text: You remember that we saw a video clip of nightly attack on the building that was shown to you previously on the photograph, that was the parliamentary building, yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the building next to the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you don't know what attack exactly is shown on the video.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you -- of course I do not know. I've seen a short video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could assist, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There are presently tendered into evidence two versions, the first version is that tendered by the Defence. The second version is that tendered by the Prosecution. Neither of those versions are very clear, certainly nowhere near as clear as that on the tape provided by Mr. Gray. The one in the booth at the moment is the tape proceeded by Mr. Gray. We will obtain a better quality copy of that hopefully in the next few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we are now playing the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, is it the Prosecution's -- will this be now the Prosecution's version that we shall see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think we play the full part of which a part has been shown by the Defence and the tape played is the original tape provided by Mr. Gray to the Defence that was then handed to the registry and not a bad copy meanwhile prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I've just been told by my case manager that in fact the visual audio booth does not have the original Gray tape. I thought it did. Perhaps we could just check with Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I'm asking because I think we have the originals and I simply wanted to know what we were about to see now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If you have the original could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not with us. We don't have it with us but our tape point 6 or 9, the very last one, is that fragment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Whereas Mr. Ierace wanted to play the complete --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does Mr. Ierace have this, I can't remember, did Mr. Ierace show this part of the tape during his cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... We would like to see the tape as well that he then refrained from it expecting that the Chamber would ask it to be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the original is in the hands of the Defence could we then please play the not perfect copy prepared by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have two original -- no, three, but we no longer know where this particular fragment is on original tapes because there's a lot of material on them and we don't know because we did a patchwork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I have never seen and neither has any other Judge in this Chamber has seen the full four videos so it's -- I think the parties should be able to identify the full part of the short clip played by the Defence. I couldn't help you to say it's on video tape 1, 2, 3 or 4. Perhaps you would know from which video you took your sequence that you showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems that from two tapes which are the BBC tapes but both are two-hours long and I'm reminding you that we did very quickly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Identified at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you wish to see the original, I think in the space of two or three minutes I could locate that in the video booth. If you wish to see the Prosecution clip, that is the one that was tendered by the Prosecution, I imagine that would probably still take us two or three minutes to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So if I could have the two original BBC tapes if you wish it, Mr. President, I could move into the video booth and find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have to -- perhaps we should have an early break, you identify them during the break and then we then start again at a quarter to 1.00. We'll adjourn until a quarter to 1.00. --- Break taken at 12:25 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, unfortunately, we cannot show the original videotape of that segment. It transpires that it is of a different system than the visual and audio booth can utilise, it's an NTSC system whereas the booth is set up for a PAL system it seems therefore that the only other complete segment that we have is the Prosecution exhibit in due course when later to the Defence provides us with the original BBC Gray tape and we retrieve from Madam Registrar the other BBC original Gray tape we will make copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think I could for the time being do without but I know that you wanted the video to be played as I said the Chamber would do, but if there's no clear copy I can put my questions to the witness also without that tape. Madam usher, would you please escort Mr. Gray into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the originals are now with the Prosecution. We'd appreciate it if they could return them to us because they belong to us and I haven't finished yet, there might be things on the tape that we are interested in, we'd like to do everything possible to copy them for ourselves and if the Prosecution wants to stop me from doing so, I don't think this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we need a clear direction on this. The Prosecution has neither original at the moment. One, I returned to the Defence at the Defence demand, I only had it for about ten minutes over the break. The other is with Madam Registrar. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a system available which would allow to copy the -- what did you say the NTSC system to PAL?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, a home video can show the NTSC video but not the booth and to qualify what I said earlier we seek access to the four original videotapes so we can make a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So all the videotapes should be put at the disposal of the registry and so that copies can be made and if there's any need to consult them we'll try and find a way that the parties can consult them.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't intend to have these cassettes tendered as such, as evidence for reasons which are --

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... At the disposal of the registry in order to be copied first it does not mean it is tendered in its entirety in the proceedings. That's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, our following witness will be a ballistics expert who is going to talk about the five shelling incidents. Given what is on these tapes, I need them as soon as possible in order to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Need them to be -- if that's true for the Defence that's true for the Prosecution, that's why they should be copied as soon as possible and I do understand that both parties have not their own facilities. They have not their own facilities at this moment to copy them so under full control of the registry, copies will be made and be put at the disposal of the parties as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties may -- the copying this way is time-consuming so therefore I invite the parties to let the Chamber -- let the registry know what video they would like to be copied first because the copying takes as much time as the video plays itself and we'll do whatever we can in order to have them copied as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the Prosecution's position is well-known. They want the first BBC tapes to be copied, I think that's what they're most interested in and I think that what remains is additional. What we are also interested in what interests us the most are also these two cassettes where we have the BBC sequences. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we start with one of the BBC cassettes copying and then the second one. So are the originals now in the hands of Madam Registrar? Could they please be provided.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have only one original tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the other four are there and I take it that it's visible that what are the BBC. Madam usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Other three, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other three, Mr. President, yes, my calculating becomes bad. Mr. Gray, we would have liked to show you the tapes again but you told us -- there are technical reasons why it could not immediately do that. You told us about the attack on the parliamentary building.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you deduce from that video image that the fire came from the east as you told us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the actual positioning of the buildings. The -- there was a photo shown to me and to the Court which was clearly taken from the Serb side of the confrontation line. The firing that appears in the videotape, you can see on the building -- on the narrow part of the building where Serb tank rounds have hit the facade of the building. Machine-gun fire which all the tracer fire is coming from the eastern side and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by the eastern side? From the right-hand side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you now talking about the photograph or on the videotape.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the videotape. The firing comes from the, as you look at it, the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is my recollection correct that it comes approximately in a horizontal line from the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slightly upwards in the firing is slightly on an angle like this it's not like this and it's not like that. It is slightly upwards. And given the calibre of the actual machine-gun being used with the tracer bullets and the actual distance that the machine-gun can physically fire with any degree of accuracy, and this was definitely aimed fire. The maximum range would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm just talking about direction rather than the range at this time.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from the eastern side and the range is important because the nearest Serb position was another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you are talking about the position. I'm just talking about the direction at this very moment. You say it came from the east.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you concluded that on the basis of what you saw on the video screen, that is, the line going slightly upwards to the left and coming from the right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, is it your position that on a two-dimensional screen, you could identify the direction from which a projectile comes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask the parties whether they would like this to be further explored? Everyone who takes a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, willingly, Mr. President, because if, for example, we have objects on a screen, objects that we know and that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are able to know whether the shot is going behind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Question whether on the basis of -- I was just trying to find out whether on the basis of the line as described by the witness, the parties would consider, apart from any additional information, whether the parties would consider that you could establish the direction where the fire comes from on the basis of the direction and the line as indicated the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say that in any event, where there are 180 degrees it's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So as a matter of fact you take it that it could be the other 180 degrees are still a possibility. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution also agrees on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we don't have to further explore the matter with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I wanted to say was that the other 180 degrees was a possibility. I think we have understood each other. I wanted to say nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within the realm of possibility, yes. Mr. Gray, you once told us that you had visited the school of theology, is that a correct understanding of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I didn't understand it as being that but that was in Nedzarici and that was on an evening after I had had meetings with the commander and the deputy commander for Nedzarici for the Serb forces in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you describe the building.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a two-storey building. It was basically being used as a medical facility when I visited it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did it -- was it one rectangular building or was it a building with several wings or --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at night and I -- from what I recall, it was a building with several wings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How many rooms did you see in that building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw one particular room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was a room close to the entry or --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the second storey that I actually went to and it was being used as a sleeping area. I mean, a dormitory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, was is it a large building.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it was quite large, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you saw a small part of it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw a very small part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you've told us about the experts that had done the expertise on the marketplace where the bomb exploded. Had you seen the crater itself?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not I trusted implicitly in the knowledge and the expertise of the officers who conducted the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Being questioned by the -- being examined by the Prosecution, you said that it was impossible that that crater could have been caused by a mortar that would have exploded on the ground but an impact that would have happened on a person, how could you be so sure about that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there would be no crater for start off if a mortar had impacted directly on a person and then exploded, there would be no crater whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it would explode on the lower extremities of a person.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It still won't leave any crater. I mean the crater that we're talking about in the marketplace was quite severe. It was a large crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have pictures been made of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean there are pictures available, I'm sure, with the BBC or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but have you seen pictures when you were reported by your experts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are pictures on the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No I'm asking whether you saw pictures when the reports came in from your experts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see them myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You more or less criticised and this as such is nothing wrong with criticising UN for sending Egypt Bat because you said they could be religiously close to one of the warring factions. Do you consider religion to be one of the forces behind the conflict or.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, definitely. It was. I mean you had Ukranian Battalion which was Orthodox Christian, you had an Egyptian Battalion who were Muslim, I mean who were the UN actually thinking about when they actually sent these battalions there? I mean the French battalion, the Canadian battalion were the ideal battalions to send there. A British battalion, a -- battalions that were ethnically and religiously fixed were -- they -- I mean the Egyptians took -- they had their compound 400 metres from the PTT and it took a pounding from the Serbs. There's no two ways about that. Ukranian Battalion, on the other hand, were at Marsal Tito barracks and they took a pounding as well. That was for a reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that your testimony is that because of their Egyptian origin that the Serbs would go harder after Egypt Bat.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And talking about origin, you're talking about religion.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about religion, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have similar experience, for example, with going after the Croats, of which I understand that the percentages of Catholics is relatively high, with going after the French for example who is supposed to be a people who is where the percentages of Catholics is relatively higher than for example in northern Europe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean the French Battalion were absolutely marvelous and they did not suffer the same amount of attrition or attacks as the Ukranians or the Egyptians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that your testimony is that the two parties involved, the Presidency sometimes referred to as Muslims and Serbs, would be driven by religious reasons to go after specifically those part of the UN forces that were of opposite religion.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Then you have given a lot of answers in respect of the apartment building in which you lived and you said that the UN flag was flying from that building.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still have that flag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How did the UN react when it became aware, and you told us that you were aware of it, that the building was used by snipers and the building was used to shield those who were at the back side of the building to get together, to group themselves.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We objected to the fact, but on the 14th of May, was really the first day of the war in Sarajevo and Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was the very first day. On the 15th of May, we basically -- we kept inside the building. It was unsafe to actually move outside the building and move anywhere. We were only located, I think, 400 metres from the PTT building. On the 16th of May, we were told to evacuate our apartment building and move to the PTT. On the 16th and 17th of May, the UNPROFOR headquarters was withdrawn from Sarajevo and they left ten military observers, 30 French soldiers and a couple of Swedish cooks and a very good Dutch communications contingent who actually kept us in contact with the rest of the world. But I mean we protested to both of the warring sides, I mean, and this was very early on that we -- I mean we didn't have the infrastructure set up with the liaison officers that we subsequently had, we didn't have them at that particular time. But we did protest about the fact that our apartment buildings, which were clearly identified with -- I mean each -- we had five apartments in the apartment buildings. Every one of them had a large UN flag flying outside it, it was clearly obvious. I mean there is a photo on the -- one of the tapes where it shows a UN vehicle which is peppered, peppered with shrapnel which came from a rifle grenade which was actually fired from within the -- within the apartment complex. I mean the building is here, the Serb forces are over here, the vehicle is here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. I do understand your testimony such that you protested at the Presidency side for using your building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We protested that they were using the building as a forming-up place to actually attack Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What was your protest against the other party? What did you protest about to the other party?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was not dealing with the other party. It was only after the 10th of June --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you told us that you protested to both parties.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The protest came from my superior, Colonel Wilson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was it about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about the fact that they were using the buildings which were occupied with civilians as a means to attack Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, that was against the Presidency forces that they used the building but now the other party.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the other party, the protest was that they were firing at buildings that were occupied with civilians and they knew that. But I mean the buildings were being used as a military installation, if you like. That's what the buildings were being used as.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why then protest or ...

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why then protest if you say, more or less, that it was a military target?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were trying to stop the fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you consider that -- or did you observe that the attacks to the apartment building did not exclude the apartments from which the UN flag was flying?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attacks on the buildings were not precise. I have a photo and I'm sorry I don't have it with me, but I have a photo of one of my officers, his name is Gwyn Reese [phoen], he was a navy lieutenant commander, the window from which he is looking has a mortar impact next to it one metre away from the actual window. He actually moved into -- and this was facing, obviously, the front line towards the Serb Nedzarici, he actually went and he slept in his bathtub because the impacts on the building were just too close. But the number of impacts that you could actually see on the actual building were maybe half a dozen, no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answer. May I just come back, very briefly, to one of your earlier answers. This video clip of the nightly attack on the parliamentary building, do you have any knowledge as where the camera would have been situated exactly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camera was probably located up -- well, I mean it would be very close to the daylight picture, the still picture that you have in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would say from the south but do you have any -- is that a reconstruction of where it should have been because I can imagine on the basis of the buildings as they appear in the picture that you would easily conclude that it's somewhere in the south but do you have any further --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then my final question is do you remember that on one of these video -- on the same video clip that you see a incendiary, at least something which seems to be flames on the, if I may say it so, the short end of the building.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you reconcile the origin of fire from the east and at the same time something hitting at least it looks as if there was a hit on that wall, I'm not suggesting there was, but at least that flames come out from the south, south-oriented wall of that building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only conclude that a tank shell had penetrated that southern side of the building and that the tracer fire, which was coming in from this direction here, had set up a fire on the inside of the building and that the flames were being seen through the actual -- I mean a tank round makes a big hole and you can see that and I can only conclude that the actual flames were coming from the inside were actually showing through one of those tank round holes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand your explanation of this picture. I have no further questions for you, Mr. Gray, but perhaps the parties would have a question. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, we no doubt have questions but meanwhile, perhaps the -- we want to ask whether the technical booth has our tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... See whether you could find it do you take the night attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the video played during the examination-in-chief and I think it was item number nine on that video, could that be brought to the technical booth and could we see whether it's possible to play that specific part and then that is not the full version, Mr. Ierace, but the limited version played before by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher -- could you please -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it it's on one of the BBC, could madam usher could assist, could you please identify on which tape we could find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring to the tape that the Defence tendered which has the excerpts played in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could perhaps -- could we see whether we -- the technicians could find the -- if you or Ms. Pilipovic could perhaps go to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it our tape?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then it is the very last clip.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record it's D348/20.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the booth runs it I'd like to ask some other questions too not to waste time. Further examination by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Gray, His Honour Judge El Mahdi asked you some questions and you answered that behind those buildings, the enemy troops got together, formed up before the attack in preparation of an attack and you are saying behind those buildings. Now, my question is if you are a military on the other side, how, with which weapon can you try to hit troops, to hit those troops which are behind those buildings? This is my first question.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most effective way would be to -- by the use of mortars but the buildings were only ten metres apart so the effect would be minimal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then concretely was there a possibility of an error in view of this small distance, perhaps that could explain shots arriving which one wouldn't have arriving?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. It's leading, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apart from that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it's not -- your question is not quite clear to me. I think the witness said that the buildings were 10 metres apart. You are talking about a small distance, a small distance to what, to the next building or to whatever?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the witness' reply. He spoke about a relatively short distance between buildings and I suppose he was speaking either about a yard or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- do you mean that by firing errors something about hitting the next building or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am speaking about firing errors because if the target is nearby then it is possible that by mistake, the projectile hits another building or something which is further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you understand this? Was this -- wasn't there a higher risk of misshots or shots going off the target because of the short distance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question, Witness, attacks on your apartment were mentioned. My question is how much time did you spend in this apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Last question it was not something which arose from the questions of the Bench and there is a question of course questions have been put but the issue has been raised already far earlier. I'll allow you to put this question to the witness, but would you please keep this in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, a question by His Honour Judge El Mahdi had to do with this UN flags and the question was why is it -- why did the commander, the [indiscernible] commanders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The Judges have not put questions in relation to issues already raised by the parties. It's not something that arose new but was an -- and it's not -- questions put by the parties to a witness after the Bench has put questions are to put questions in respect of issues not raised by the parties before. That cannot be said of this subject but I'll allow you to seek the answer of the witness on this respect but just for the coming 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and so Witness, did you spend a lot of time in this part, how much time did you spend in that apartment daily?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I arrived in Sarajevo on the 10th of April, 1992. I was appointed as the chief of operations for all military observers in the former Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, if I may interrupt you, the question was how much time a day you'd spend in the apartment, approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maximum of eight hours, maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, perhaps we can all try to see the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Episode of the Defence video has been located we could look at it again. If the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you fast forward because this is not what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps quickly move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it seems if there is nothing after this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Backwards. For the information of the video booth it's a clip in which a nightly attack is shown but if you have any other questions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we could -- I think, yes. Yes, I think we have come to the part if it could be rewound, rewind, backwards, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you, like I did, see -- but I don't want --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, but I haven't yet asked my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you started your question saying have you seen as I did, and that could only result in explaining to the witness what you saw. But now we have a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, have you well been able to observe the video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you see certain bullets hit the facade of the building, the long wall of the building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see other projectiles going off the mark?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that -- of seeing anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then see once again the tape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we could play it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it would be rewound.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And witness, I'd appreciate it if you attentively watch this tape for possible projectiles which did not hit their targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you watch closely and therefore see some projectiles which, perhaps, missed their targets?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we then look at the location of the buildings on the one hand, and on the other, on the basis of your personal knowledge of Sarajevo, could you tell us, confirm or rather know what is said about the origin of these projectiles?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firing was from a -- what I would call a medium machine-gun, 7.92 calibre. The firing rate and the actual sound --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. This is material that was covered in chief, let alone the fact that it wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but apart that from, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I asked both parties whether it was of any use to continue asking questions about what could be seen on a two-dimensional screen and the parties agreed, I refer to you mentioning 180 degrees that just from such a line you can't draw any conclusions. You are now asking the witness to draw conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, I don't agree. What I said was that one could exclude 180 too, but keep the 120s and on the base of the field of vision one can establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... To establish to you could exclude that it come from the other short side of the building but there's still such a range possible that where the witness testified that he has his knowledge only from this video and has no specific knowledge, neither where the camera was nor of the event itself, that whatever conclusions you ask him to make as to the source of fire will suffer from the same problem we saw before and if --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- precise questions then please put them but you asked him whether he could say anything on the source of fire and I'm quite willing during the break to explain to the parties--

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Then I will ask a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say that you saw these projectiles which missed the targets in relation to the short wall, the short facade that is, the north/south one where we could see those tank marks. How would you follow the trajectories of these projectiles, would you say that they were flying in parallel with this south wall or were they falling perpendicularly to the south wall, for instance, along the axis of the tank marks, what can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few small rounds that went past the building went past the south wall and they were slightly, as I said before, they were slightly rising in angle as opposed to going down in angle which is within what I would expect for a weapon of this type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with regard to the flames on the south wall which we saw on the tape, does that confirm what you said or does this contradict what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the flames were clearly coming through a hole in the wall on the short axis, the southern axis of the building and they were -- flames from clearly coming from the inside out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my very last question: Following the question by Judge El Mahdi you said something that was new, you said that the two officers whom you sent to that market was actually then engaging in their first investigation; however, on another page in the transcript, you said the following and I will quote you in English: I sent two very experienced officers. [Interpretation] So my question is as follows: Where did these officers gain this experience because obviously that was their first job of this kind in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very experienced officers in their own field. One was a very experienced Australian major in artillery. He had been a battery commander until he came to Sarajevo, and prior to him coming to Sarajevo, he had been with United Nations truce supervisory organisation in Palestine. The Canadian captain was very experienced in mortar operations. He was a mortar platoon commander and he was very experienced in what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace. Any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in relation to the apartment building in which you were living was shelled, that you protested to the Presidency forces and you said in response to a question regarding protests to the Serb side, "At that time I was not dealing with the other party." Do you remember that you told us that on the 18th of May, 1992, you spoke to the deputy commander of the Serbs in Nedzarici together with one of his lieutenants and the deputy commander spoke excellent English and you discussed with him the shelling of the apartment building? Firstly, do you remember that you said that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Secondly, did you protest to him at all about the shelling of the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had neighbours there at that stage and I was extremely upset that the apartment buildings had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said in relation to the shelling of the market, "There are --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in relation to the explosion of the market?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the if you could just shortly, briefly indicate what your objection is based upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it was very clear repeatedly Mr. Ierace repeats this word of shelling and I said no because the witness was speaking about bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Page 86, line 10 and perhaps it might have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but my objection was this and I don't mind when I am repeating things but not everything because that is wearisome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The testimony of the witness was that there was an explosion rather than a shell that landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in relation to the explosion at the market, in particular, in relation to the crater, "There are pictures on the videotape." Now, when did you last see on those videotapes that you've given us a image of that crater, when did you last see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it for days because I mean I haven't had the -- I mean the tapes have been in the possession of the Defence counsel ever since I have arrived here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you saw it on the videotapes since you have been here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time that you saw it on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Years ago now, years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you confident that there is somewhere on those four videotapes some footage which shows that crater?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am pretty confident, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the four videotapes, one shows three television programmes from New Zealand dealing with the training and experience of New Zealand peace-keeping forces in Croatia in 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. This is this has absolutely nothing to do with the questions asked by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in response to one of your questions, the witness has said for the first time that somewhere on the videotape there is an image showing the crater and I wish to clarify where on those videotapes the crater is and if possible, over night, have the witness review the videotapes and locate that image. And I think we can eliminate some of the videotapes by this questioning as being ones on which that image might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your question is to identify the possible videotape on which this picture might appear. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to, in my view, this question lacks completely foundation and the market scene was -- this matter was raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Further identify that part of the video on which the crater appears. That is the purpose of this question and the appearance of the crater in a video is, I think, something that appeared -- that came up during questioning by the Bench. So the objection is denied please proceed but in this line, Mr. Ierace, not of anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So one of the tapes has some television programmes produced in New Zealand in 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember having a tape with that on it, a documentary on New Zealand television about peace-keeping forces from New Zealand in Croatia in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could we please try to finish because there is a videolink necessary this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be prepared to go through the videotapes overnight and locate firstly the image of the crater?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. One doesn't really know where the tapes are and they are in the hands of the registry they need to be copied, an impossible question is asked and besides it is absolutely beyond the scope of the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The Prosecution wants to identify the tape on which a crater appears on which the witness testified it was on the video and where I do understand that the Prosecution has difficulties in locating it. The only question was first of all about the willingness of the witness and whether it would be practically possible is another issue. Would you be willing to review videos overnight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I've given sufficient evidence of this whole incident. I mean we have been over this incident many, many times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was I do understand if you say I'm too tired to do it then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can look through the tapes. I just need a facility to actually view the tapes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You stated that you are willing, if really necessary, that's how I understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace but please keep in mind we really have to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the only remaining aspect is in relation to the video we saw on the Defence tape of the Ukrainian I think, it was a radar facility and the second segment on the Defence tape, a conversation with some soldiers in the forest. Whilst the witness checks -- please if I could finish my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let Mr. Ierace first speak what he wants to ask or to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if while the witness reviews the tapes, in order to locate the crater, he could also inform us tomorrow if he has located the tape with those two segments on it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it would be any tomorrow, Mr. Ierace, that's because all questions have been put to the witness and -- let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I think that too much is being asked of this witness but it's not up to me to say that and also from the Defence, I remind you that these tapes we need -- those of the market because we shall need them in the examination of our next witness and what we are saying now that if tapes are now blocked somewhere, then we cannot use them so that I will need a day off tomorrow in order to be able to prepare my examination. It's up to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm not asking you to come back but just to know when you are about to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am here for at least another day, sir, and I am available if you would like to see me, I'm available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, it's up to the parties to try and find a way through the videos, that's point one. If the witness can assist and I do understand that if necessary, he's willing to assist, then nevertheless first priority should be given to copying of the videotapes which will take presumably until tomorrow. I take it that once a copy has been made that an extra copy so that both parties have one is easily produced. Well, all the practical aspects of copying the videotapes is a different matter but that gets full priority and if there will be remaining time through the intervention of the registry and the Victims and Witness Unit, we might ask, if possible, and then it will be written down by the party who wants to have located a certain part of a video and we'll then invite the witness to just write down on a piece of paper where he located the part asked for so that he doesn't have to reappear in court. I think it's just a practical matter on to help the parties find a way through these videos that have been delivered rather late. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'll do it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, you have been in this courtroom and in the other courtroom for quite some time. We are fully aware of that. The Chamber is also aware that your health circumstances were not ideal to travel to The Hague and nevertheless you took the effort to come and to respond to the call of the Defence to appear as a witness. You have answered many, many questions of both parties and of the Bench. I'd like to thank you very, very much for coming, for testifying, and perhaps even do some extra work tomorrow. We'll see whether this is necessary and whether it can be done or not, but then finally, I hope that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when the witness leaves then I'll like to have a word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep it briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course but one thing, if we need to see the tape and the witness has finished --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If this will be done, the witness will have a little piece of paper saying could you locate and then the sequences and then he can do it alone and he'll report to say so to the registrar so that the registrar will then transfer to the parties whatever information the witness gives.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second question is am I nevertheless authorised to see the witness because he has finished? I talk not about this, but perhaps merely as a gesture, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we have -- the only thing we ask from the witness is to locate certain --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And my third point, and I have to indicate immediately these tapes which is necessary -- are necessary for the second witness so problems, delay, and request for a possible postponement if necessary, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar again informs me that we -- the Chamber should not promise anything because the technical difficulties in copying are considerable. I think the Chamber did not promise anything apart from that we would give full priority and that as far as the Chamber is concerned we would do our utmost best to give the best possible results.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning same courtroom.
